extracted.intended_audience: judges, patent litigators, representatives and court staff before the Unified Patent Court (UPC)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and interpretive principles governing conduct of proceedings before the Unified Patent Court, including priorities among instruments, core principles (proportionality, flexibility, fairness/equity), case management objectives, timelines and duties of parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy of applicable instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall conduct proceedings in accordance with the Agreement, the Statute and these Rules. In the event of a conflict between the provisions of the Agreement and/or the Statute on the one hand and of the Rules on the other hand, the provisions of the Agreement and/or the Statute shall prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying these Rules, the Agreement and the Statute take precedence; any inconsistency must be resolved in favour of the Agreement/Statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation in accordance with specific Agreement articles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules shall be applied and interpreted in accordance with Articles 41(3), 42 and 52(1) of the Agreement on the basis of the principles of proportionality, flexibility, fairness and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation must follow the cited Agreement articles and be guided explicitly by the enumerated principles; these form the interpretive lens for procedural questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of proportionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportionality shall be ensured by giving due consideration to the nature and complexity of each action and its importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case management, procedural steps and allocation of resources should be scaled to the nature, complexity and importance of the case; avoid disproportionate procedures for simple matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Flexibility shall be ensured by applying all procedural rules in a flexible and balanced manner with the required level of discretion for the judges to organise the proceedings in the most efficient and cost effective manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges have discretion to adapt procedures to the needs of the case to promote efficiency and cost-effectiveness; rigid application of rules where flexibility would be appropriate is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of fairness and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness and equity shall be ensured by having regard to the legitimate interests of all parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and judicial decisions must consider and protect the legitimate interests of each party to ensure fair and equitable treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective to ensure decisions of the highest quality
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with these principles, the Court shall apply and interpret the Rules in a way which shall ensure decisions of the highest quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application and interpretation of procedural rules should aim to produce well-reasoned, high-quality judicial outcomes; procedural choices that would undermine quality are to be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness objective for first-instance oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings shall be conducted in a way which will normally allow the final oral hearing on the issues of infringement and validity at first instance to take place within one year whilst recognising that complex actions may require more time and procedural steps and simple actions less time and fewer procedural steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The default planning expectation is an oral hearing within one year, but flexibility exists for complex or simple cases; timelines for decisions on costs and/or damages may be concurrent with the main decision or as soon as practicable thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-management organised to meet objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Case management shall be organised in accordance with these objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All case-management measures should be designed to implement proportionality, flexibility, fairness/equity, quality and timeliness objectives; case management is the tool to achieve these aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' duty to cooperate and early disclosure of full case
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall cooperate with the Court and set out their full case as early as possible in the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are expected actively to assist efficient case management by cooperating and presenting their complete case early; failure to do so may conflict with proportionality and timeliness objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of application and interpretation across divisions and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court shall endeavour to ensure consistent application and interpretation of these Rules by all first instance divisions and the Court of Appeal. Due consideration shall also be given to this objective in any decision concerning leave to appeal against procedural orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for uniformity across different divisions and in appellate leave decisions; consistency is a factor when considering permissions to appeal procedural orders.
